scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports, from the 2026-11-23 symbol-level re-audit (method in structural-audit-2026-11-23.md).

findings.group: Structure: Go's shape before more ports
findings.finding: Go's unistore serves RPCs concurrently: `Server.KvCommit` (and every other handler) calls `MVCCStore` with no server-wide lock, and `MVCCStore.Commit` / `Prewrite` serialize only on the region's key-hash latches (`regCtx.AcquireLatches`), so client-go's 16 KB commit batches (`calcActionConcurrency`, up to `CommitterConcurrency` = 128) run in parallel. The Rust `KvHandler` takes `&mut self` and every RPC goes through one `Mutex<KvHandler>`, so all batches commit one after another. Measured 2026-11-28: a 50k-row insert's 100k secondary keys commit in 259 ms (40k keys in 120 ms; raising the client's commit concurrency from 16 to 128 changes nothing), while Go master's ANALYZE, started 25-65 ms after the same insert, always sees every row. Read-committed readers (ANALYZE) therefore miss rows Go's see: `tests_planner_core_integration_seek_cost`'s `analyze` re-runs ANALYZE until `stats_meta.count` matches, which Go's TestIndexScanSeekCost does not need.
